topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE INTO TOPSCHOLAR, found 4 September 2026
note: TopSCHOLAR's file endpoint /cgi/viewcontent.cgi refuses every script and even headless Chrome with a 403; the block is on the TLS fingerprint. The Internet Archive has mirrored those same PDFs and serves them to plain curl. Fetching http://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=<N>&context=dlsc_ua_records returned a real 4.6 MB Herald issue on the first try. Get <N> from the record page, which curl CAN read with -L: it carries the viewcontent link. The `id_` in the wayback path matters, it asks for the raw file rather than the archive's HTML wrapper. USE curl -L. Without it the Wayback URL returns a bare 302 and an empty file. The embedded text layer varies by era and the earlier claim here was too broad: it is close to unreadable on the 1990s and 2005 scans, where you should render at 300 dpi with PyMuPDF and run ocrmac instead, but on the 2002-2009 Heralds it is GOOD and far better than OCR. Test the text layer before spending hours OCRing. This opens every scanned Herald and Talisman on TopSCHOLAR to plain scripts and removes the reason _topscholar-wanted.json existed.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE, SECOND URL FORM

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE HAS A CONCURRENCY CEILING
note: web.archive.org serves these PDFs at roughly 0.5 to 1 MB/s per connection and will accept about four connections from one address. A fifth gets 'Failed to connect to web.archive.org port 80' rather than an HTTP error, and a harvester that treats that as a missing snapshot will silently skip real issues. Run three or four workers, never more; give curl --connect-timeout 25 --speed-time 25 --speed-limit 20000; and on curl exit codes 7, 28, 35, 52 or 56 back off twenty seconds and retry the SAME url rather than falling through to the /context/.../type/native/viewcontent form, which costs another timeout. Never mark an issue done on a failed fetch. Sustained pulling for an hour or two visibly slows the whole thing down, so plan the run long rather than wide.

topic: WAYBACK: PARALLEL RANGE REQUESTS BEAT A SINGLE STREAM BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE
note: The 2016 Talisman is 755,645,090 bytes and a single curl was pulling it at about 30 KB/s after an hour of sustained use, which would have taken another hour. web.archive.org honours HTTP Range on these files. Ask for one byte with -r 0-0 -D - and the response carries content-range: bytes 0-0/755645090, which gives you the true size; then split the remainder into four ranges and fetch them in parallel with curl -r a-b. The last 111 MB came down in about two minutes, exact byte counts, and concatenating them onto the truncated file produced a PDF that opens cleanly. Use this for any Talisman; four ranges is within the concurrency ceiling.

Four of the 107 are roster fragments rather than names, leaving 103 people. 65 of the 103 (63 per cent) are named in the paper at least once. 18 (17 per cent) are certainly inside a printed frame, meaning a caption names them. 6 (6 per cent) are in a frame where their own position is provable and the face is legible. So the answer is that the Herald DID write about most of them and did NOT photograph them: two in five never appear at all, and of those who are photographed two thirds are in frames that identify nobody - a night silhouette, an overhead shot of the tops of two heads, a figure forty halftone dots wide across a road, a crowd caption naming three people and positioning none. Expect roughly ONE PORTRAIT PER SIXTEEN SENATORS from a full pass over the other eight blocks, about forty faces in all. That is worth doing, but plan it as a bulk exercise on the two sources that carry labelled frames (the opinion-page poll strip and the spring candidate page), not as a page-by-page hunt: reading news photographs one at a time produced two usable faces out of about seventy pages opened on this run.

topic: A CHEAP WAY TO ASK 'IS THERE A PHOTOGRAPH ON THIS PAGE, AND IS THIS NAME UNDER IT'
note: Two techniques that made the difference between opening 70 pages and opening 500, worth reusing on any newsprint block. FIRST, detect halftone photographs without OCR: render the page at 100 dpi greyscale, take the fraction of pixels below 140 in each 16-pixel block, and threshold at 0.36. Newsprint body text sits at about 0.17, headlines about 0.3, halftone photographs 0.45 to 0.8, blank paper 0.0. Close the mask once and take connected components larger than five blocks square. That separates photographs from type reliably on 1993-2005 Heralds and tells you in a second whether a page has any picture at all - on this run it killed a dozen leads outright because the page turned out to carry nothing but advertisements. SECOND, and cheaper still because it needs no PDF: a name is probably in a CAPTION if a photographer credit token ('/Herald', 'photo by', 'Photos by') sits on the same page within 0.10 of the page height ABOVE it and roughly the same column. Run that over the OCR alone and 1,027 raw name hits reduce to 149 caption-zone candidates. Both are in /tmp/hunt-n9701b but that will not survive; they are four dozen lines each and are described here so they can be rewritten.

topic: WHAT SEPARATES A POLL LABEL FROM A LETTER SIGNATURE: MEASURE THE PAGE, NOT THE TEXT
note: The single most useful thing learned on the bulk pass, and the reason six false hits were reported once before. On the Herald's Opinion page the People Poll label and the LETTER SIGNATURE are set in exactly the same way - name in bold, home town and class in italic beneath it - so no amount of text analysis will tell them apart, and clustering does not save you either: three Young Democrats co-signing one letter on 30 January 1996 look precisely like three poll entries in a row. THE TEST THAT WORKS is the photograph. Render the page grey at about 110 dpi, walk upward from the label in strips 0.004 of page height deep across the label's own column, and take the fraction of pixels below 140. Newsprint body type sits near 0.17, a headline near 0.3, a halftone photograph between 0.45 and 0.8, blank paper at 0. Four consecutive dark strips is a frame; anything less is the letter's own body text. On this run that test turned 85 name matches into 18 real frames in a few minutes and every one of the rejects was confirmed by eye afterwards. Second warning: what sits above a letter signature is very often a CARTOON, which is halftone-dark too, so always look at the crop before cutting - Alex Rose (a David Koresh cartoon), Lena Sweeten-Garner, Robert Reynolds, Bob Bell and Matt Bogard all pass a naive darkness test and none is a portrait.

detail: Supersedes every name-by-name index lookup in these two volumes. Both books were opened whole, all 84 portrait grid pages were read, and 1,982 name labels were parsed off them with their cell positions (1,047 in 1993, 935 in 1994). The back indexes were re-OCR'd COLUMN BY COLUMN at 5x because the pooled page OCR reads four-column index pages badly - the previously stored 1993 index had a hole running straight from Seebold to Templeton and lost the whole Sh-Sm-St-Ta run, every Smith included. Complete now: 1,739 index entries for 1993 and 1,240 for 1994, continuous through the alphabet. GRID PAGES. 1993: 20-21 graduates, 24-46 seniors, 48-54 juniors, 56-62 sophomores, 63-74 freshmen, 76-80 faculty and staff; the TOP OF THE HILL feature pages at 25, 31, 35, 39, 47, 51, 55, 59, 67, 71, 75 carry no portraits. 1994: 22-47 by residence hall then Off-Campus, 57-70 by greek chapter, 79-80 faculty and staff. LAYOUT, read off the page images and not assumed. 1993 is FOUR across and five rows deep, twenty names in ONE COLUMN down the LEFT margin in blocks of four against each grid row, alphabetical left to right (p. 78 block two: Anna Jo Johnson, Horace Johnson Jr., Cynthia Y. Jones, Kaveh Khatir against faces F M F M). 1994 is FIVE across and six rows deep, thirty names in ONE COLUMN down the RIGHT margin in blocks of five, alphabetical left to right, and the alphabet RESTARTS mid-page at each new chapter heading, so never read the order across a heading (pp. 59 and 63 both do this). RESULT against all 134 people with no portrait whose first SGA year falls 1992-93 to 1996-97: SIX appear anywhere in either volume and TWO crops came out of it, both flagged FACE PROVED PERSON NOT PROVED - Nicki Jerome as "Nicki Gerome Jr." on 1994 p. 63 Sigma Kappa row 1 cell 1, and Crystal Smith on 1994 p. 59 Alpha Omicron Pi row 6 cell 3. The other four are dead: Horace Johnson is photographed at 1993 p. 78 but he is WKU's Public Safety Director and campus police chief, not an SGA officer (the Herald letter of 13 Feb 1996 that is the archive's only source for him says 'campus police Chief Horace Johnson' outright); Edward Myers and Cinnamon Roberts are both in the 1993 ASG group photograph at p. 204 with a full printed row key and are unusable at 15 to 18 pixels a face; Alex Rose is photographed twice, 1993 p. 109 from directly overhead showing only the top of his head and 1994 p. 23 with his face only as a reflection in a hand mirror, mouth open. WHY SO THIN, and this is the structural finding: the 1994 volume is the LAST book with portrait grids and it covers 1993-94. Of the 134 targets, 87 have a first SGA year of 1995-96 or 1996-97, and NOT ONE of those 87 is anywhere in either book - they were still in high school or unphotographed first-years when the last grid book went to press. Neither book photographs the whole student body either: about 1,047 and 935 portraits against a student body near 15,000, so roughly one student in fifteen. DO NOT SEND ANOTHER AGENT AT THESE TWO VOLUMES FOR THE 1995-97 COHORT. Both PDFs are already on disk at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_topscholar-pdfs/, archive.org holds no 1993 or 1994 Talisman (its WKU run stops at 1987), and the full page-by-page OCR plus both re-OCR'd indexes are in _talisman-ocr-1993-1994. Native resolution is 864 by 1152 pixels per printed page for 1993 and 816 by 1123 for 1994, which is why group photographs are hopeless and grid cells come out 100 to 155 pixels.

name: How to read a WKU composite roster without a single download
detail: TWO THINGS THAT WILL SAVE THE NEXT RUN AN HOUR. FIRST, data/herald-index-full.json ALREADY CONTAINS EVERY COMPOSITE ROSTER. It is not only a Herald index: it covers dlsc_ua_records 1-9992, all 645 stu_org items and twenty other collections, and for a composite the stored 'lines' are the landing-page abstract, which IS the roster. Grep it before fetching anything: `Members of the <year> <programme> class:` is the exact opening. The catch is the 300-character cap this repository already documents - 95 of the 116 nursing and dental hygiene roster lines are truncated mid-name - so the local copy is enough to decide WHETHER to look and not enough to match on. SECOND, when you do need the full roster, fetch the LANDING PAGE, not the PDF, with plain curl and a browser user-agent; digitalcommons serves landing pages to scripts without complaint at one request every 2.5 seconds. But DO NOT read the roster out of `<meta name="description">`: bepress truncates that tag at exactly 300 characters too, which silently reproduces the same defect. The complete roster is in the page body at `<div id='abstract' class='element'>`, in SINGLE quotes, which is why a double-quoted regex finds nothing. 150 landing pages came down this way in about six minutes with no 403. ROSTER FORMAT VARIES AND WILL BREAK A NAIVE PARSER. Nursing and dental hygiene print 'First Last, First Last'. The Spirit Masters booklets and the physical therapy yearbook print 'Last, First Last, First' with the surname leading and the commas in the middle of each pair, so splitting on commas silently produces names that never existed - 'Alyson Manley' out of 'Manley, Alyson Manley, Ashlee'. Detect it by whether the first comma-chunk after the colon is a single word. WHAT IS ON DISK FOR THE NEXT RUN, outside /tmp: ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_composite-rosters/ holds rosters.json, the complete untruncated abstract, PDF url, file size and discipline for all 150 composite records; sm_people.json, the 219 Spirit Masters split out one per person with name, role, class year and the full biography text; and parse2.py, the parser that handles both roster orders. Re-matching a new name list against the whole source class costs one script run and no network at all.

All 19 club pages, printed 369-387, were OCR'd and every group key parsed and matched against everyone in the archive without a face. **Two faces, and they are the only two there are**: Drew Mitchell from the Public Relations Student Society of America on p. 382 and Sunetris Fluellen from Delta Sigma Theta on p. 374. Do not reopen it.
  The rule that decides these: **a club key is only usable when the group is small enough that rows can be told apart.** The fraternity and sorority pages name a hundred or more people in one alphabetical run with no row markers at all — Kelly Simmons sits in an Alpha Omicron Pi list of that kind and Eileen Forsythe in Phi Mu, and neither can ever be cut from them. The row-keyed groups of thirty or more are just as useless because the faces fall below twenty pixels.
  Where a row assignment is genuinely ambiguous, **occlusion settles it and head height does not.** On the PRSSA photograph the sexes named in the key admit two different readings, and what fixed Drew Mitchell was that his shoulders are overlapped on both sides by the two people in front of him. On Delta Sigma Theta the counts forced it outright: the key's rows run two, three and four, and the tiers hold two, three and four.

name: Six 2012 Talisman grid cells: Julia Payne, Sarah Hazelip, Brenna Duncan, Jonathon Tabor, Katie Martin, Lucy George
detail: Published 8 September from the 2012 Talisman class grids. The CELL is proved in every case, by the group's alphabetical order and its sex pattern against the printed row, which is the method this project trusts. What is missing is the second test the twenty-eight faces published from the all-volumes sweep the same night all carried: neither the volume's back index nor any ASG page is cited to show the student in the grid is the SGA person of that name. Katie Martin is the partial exception - she is in the graduate section and sat as Senator for Graduate Students, which is consistent but is not an index citation. Names like Katie Martin, Julia Payne and Lucy George carry a real collision risk in a volume of this size. NOT CUT, and a later pass must not cut them either on a failed search: the 2012 volume is not on archive.org - the identifier talisman2012west returns 503 - so the index could not be opened from here, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a miss proves nothing. WHAT TO DO: open dlsc_ua_records/8897, read the back index for each of the six, and record either the index line tying the name to an ASG page or the fact that the volume carries only one person of that name. Also worth settling while there: Jonathon Tabor and Lucy George are filed to 2009-10 off an underclassmen grid covering 2011-12, which works only if the grid runs to juniors.

kind: route blocked from the cloud container, and what it does NOT prove
name: The Wayback route into TopSCHOLAR, retested 8 September 2026
detail: Tried to discharge the VERIFICATION OWED on the six 2012 Talisman grid cells (Julia Payne, Sarah Hazelip, Brenna Duncan, Jonathon Tabor, Katie Martin, Lucy George) and could not, for a reason worth writing down so the next run does not spend the same time on it. The record page dlsc_ua_records/8897 reads fine from the cloud container over plain curl and gives article=9884. Both TopSCHOLAR's own /cgi/viewcontent.cgi and the documented Wayback route then failed, but NOT in the same way and NOT for the reason the WAYBACK ROUTE INTO TOPSCHOLAR entry above describes: web.archive.org is refused by the cloud container's own egress policy, one attempt returning the literal body 'Blocked by egress policy' and later ones dying as connection resets, which the agent proxy logged against web.archive.org:443 as tunnel closed mid-exchange. So the route is not broken; this environment cannot reach the host it needs. The file is definitely there: archive.org/wayback/available IS reachable and reports a status-200 snapshot of article 9884 taken 8 July 2024 (timestamp 20240708084113). A run on a machine that can reach web.archive.org should get it on the first try. One further narrowing while the record page was open: its description is an index of the volume's FEATURE STORIES and their bylines, not of the students pictured, so the landing page alone can never settle the six and there is no point re-reading it. The back index inside the PDF is still the thing to open. NONE OF THIS IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SIX. They stay published, as the 8 September editor's pass ruled: a route that could not be travelled proves nothing about what lies at the end of it, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a miss is never grounds for a cut.

kind: run re-confirms the queue is empty; the two 'dead ends' corrected on review
name: 8 September 2026, second photograph run of the day
detail: Independently re-ran the priority checks the prior run of the same day recorded, rather than trusting its commit message: programmatically confirmed all four named presidents (Nick Todd, Katie Dawson, Jeanne Johnson, Reagan Gilley) have a photos.json leader entry, that every leaders[] role containing 'president' or 'regent' across all 61 years has one too (72 terms, zero misses), and that every one of the 61 years has at least one photograph (leader portrait or years[] entry). Re-checked on the editor's pass of 8 September and all three hold exactly. The two leads this run first wrote up as dead ends are NOT dead, and the editor's pass corrected them rather than let a wrong conclusion stand where the next run would read it. (1) The block on the Lisa Kappler chief justice resignation story, Herald 17 Feb 2009 (dlsc_ua_records/6721, viewcontent.cgi?article=7724), is not specific to that article. A control fetch of an unrelated article (viewcontent.cgi?article=5695) returned the identical 403 bot-check page, the same 151,141 bytes, so what is blocked from this container is the viewcontent.cgi route as a whole. Landing pages are unaffected: dlsc_ua_records/6721 returned 200 and its own index names the story, Barczak on the SGA chief justice resigning. Do not record a viewcontent 403 as evidence about a particular document again. (2) The Wayback route is not blocked from this container and should be the first fallback whenever viewcontent.cgi refuses. Checked 8 September: web.archive.org and archive.org/wayback/available both returned 200, the availability API reports a snapshot of article 7724 taken 21 July 2024, and the timestamped id_ replay URL delivered the full issue PDF, 13,418,383 bytes beginning %PDF. The recipe is web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<the blocked viewcontent URL>. The Kappler lead is therefore live and retrievable, and the six 2012 Talisman grid cells still carrying a verification owed should be retried by this route. The PDF's text layer did not extract in this container, so nothing has been read out of the file yet and no claim rests on it. (3) The 1994 and 1995 Talisman are genuinely not on archive.org, but the 503 the run first recorded did not show that: archive.org was up on re-test (talisman1975west returned 200) and talisman1994west and talisman1995west returned 404, which is the absence the conclusion needed. A 503 is a service that is down, never proof a volume is not held. No portraits were added this run.

kind: lead closed: article read, no photograph exists
name: Lisa Kappler chief justice resignation, retrieved via Wayback
detail: Followed the editor's pass recipe (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<the blocked viewcontent.cgi URL>) and it worked: the snapshot taken 21 Jul 2024 (timestamp 20240721095749) delivered the full issue PDF, 13,418,383 bytes, opening with %PDF-1.7. Extracted with pymupdf (installed fresh into this container; neither pymupdf nor pdftotext nor any PDF CLI was actually present despite SGA-60-AGENT-INFO.md's note that PyMuPDF is installed). The story is on page 4 of the PDF (printed 'Page 3'), headline 'SGA chief justice resigns' by Mary Barczak, confirming the text already summarized in this file: Kappler resigned 12 Feb 2009, President Kayla Shelton needed a replacement before the 24-25 Feb student regent special election, Executive VP Skylar Jordan and associate justice Corey Bewley commented. But there is no photograph attached to it: every image on the page was located by bounding box (15 raster images total) and every one falls either to the right of x=460 (the adjoining Relay For Life sidebar and a financial-aid photo) or below y=497 (the stimulus-bill story further down the page); the Kappler article's own text occupies only x=44-455, y=92-490, and no image bbox overlaps that region. It is a text-only story. This lead is closed, not just retried: the PDF is now provably readable from this container, and it provably contains no Kappler portrait. Do not re-open it looking for an image that was never there.

kind: VERIFICATION OWED discharged, one misidentification found and fixed
name: The six 2012 Talisman grid cells, retrieved via Wayback and checked against the back index
detail:
Discharged the verification owed on Julia Payne, Sarah Hazelip, Brenna Duncan, Jonathon Tabor, Katie Martin and Lucy George by the route the editor's pass reopened. The 2012 Talisman (dlsc_ua_records/8897, article=9884) is a 404-page, 740,936,167-byte scan with a text layer on its single TopSCHOLAR cover page only - every one of the other 403 pages is image-only, so the back index had to be read visually, page by page, at 6x zoom (a first pass at 1.2x misread two entries and both were caught by re-zooming: 'Tabor, Jonathon 366, 372' first read as '372, 382', and 'George, Lucy 354' first read as '364' - low-resolution index reads are not reliable and should always be re-verified at high zoom before being written down). All six now check out exactly against the printed index: Payne 362 & 381, Hazelip 356 & 374, Duncan 353 & 382, Tabor 366 & 372, Martin 333 (single page, matching the prior note that she is a graduate-section exception), George 354 (single page). Every published page number matches one of the index's own page numbers for that name - no article citation was needed because the index itself now confirms the CELL's page.
  Better than that: the underclassmen and seniors grids on these pages turn out to be captioned in print, a row of names running down the margin beside each row of four (underclassmen) or three (seniors) photos, top-to-bottom matching left-to-right - the earlier 'alphabetical order and sex pattern' method was solid but indirect where a much stronger check was sitting on the same page unread. Checked Duncan (p.354), Hazelip (p.356) and Payne (p.362) against their printed captions and the row-and-column position named by the caption is exactly the file already published for each. Tabor's own page (p.366) carries his name in print beside his photo, independent of the index and the row/column method both.
  Katie Martin's did not check out. Her row on p.333 (seniors) reads MAE MARCHIONE / NANCY MARSHALL / KATIE MARTIN against three photos left to right, and the third position - a woman with glasses, a white scarf and light brown hair - is who the caption names. The file published as 2012-13-katie-martin.jpg was none of the three women in that row: a fourth face entirely, not Marchione, not Marshall, not the captioned Martin. Checked it against Marchione (glasses, pearls, blue jacket), Marshall (no glasses, dark top) and against Lanika Mayes and Mildred Maradiaga on the same page in case of a one-row slip - none matched, and its md5 doesn't match any other file in data/photos/, so it wasn't a copy-paste of a different published leader either. Wherever it came from, it was not Katie Martin. Re-cropped the actual captioned cell (p.333, row 3, column 3) and replaced data/photos/2012-13-katie-martin.jpg with it; verified the new file opens as a real JPEG (FF D8 FF) at 1132x1344. This is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md's photo rules exist to catch - a face that could not be confirmed from its caption was published anyway, at some point before this file's own record of the six begins - and the fix is to trust the caption, not the row proximity a prior pass assumed.

Cross-referenced organization.executive and organization.senate.officers against photos.json leaders and got the same ~221-row gap list the second run recorded, checked it against _officers-truly-missing-2026-09-06.json and confirmed 216 of those rows are already in it (i.e. already hunted).
  Of the handful not on that list, spent the run's search budget on names in years archive.org actually holds (1974-75, 1977-78, 1978-79, 1980-81, 1986-87) using the item's own full-text search API (https://<server>/fulltext/inside.php?item_id=...&doc=...&path=...&q="<exact phrase>") to get a page number, then pulling that leaf as a JPEG via BookReaderImages.php and reading it directly. Results: Vern Pulman (1974-75, representative-at-large) has no Talisman mention at all - his only source is a Herald appointment notice, consistent with no yearbook photo existing. Alice Wicks (1978-79, secretary) likewise has zero Talisman hits; her record is Herald-only. David Young (1978-79, administrative vice president) has exactly one Talisman hit, a text mention on the article page the archive already cites (pp.288-289) with no accompanying photograph - checked the actual leaves (288, 289, 290) and the only individual portrait on that spread is president Steve Thornton's, already published. David Bass (1977-78, activities vice president) is named in a real caption ('A LIGHT MOMENT IN AN ASG MEETING brings laughter from president Bob Moore and smiles from activities vice president David Bass, secretary Sharon May and vice president Cathy Murphy') over a candid group photo, but the photo shows at most three clearly visible people for four named subjects and there is no way to tell which face is Bass's with confidence - left unpublished rather than guess; this is a real lead, not a dead end, for a pass with more time to study the print at higher resolution or find a second photo of him. Steve Wilson (1978-79, judicial council chairman) turned up three hits, all either an SAE fraternity Spring Sing story or a senior-directory line reading 'STEVE WILSON, agriculture' with no ASG context - a common name and too weak a link to publish per the no-surname-matching rule; also not closed, just not usable this run. Mark Chesnut (1980-81, treasurer), Chris Millay (1986-87, parliamentarian) and Dwight Austin (1986-87, sergeant-at-arms) all returned zero hits in their respective archive.org volumes.
  Also live-tested the two names the second run of the day left open pending 'TopSCHOLAR access to spare' - Jacob Miers (2007-08/2008-09 Secretary of the Senate, sourced only to SGA meeting minutes) and Eddie/Edward Myers (1994-95 Student Athletic Committee chair). A site:digitalcommons.wku.edu web search for each (the CLAUDE.md-recommended workaround for TopSCHOLAR's blocked search page) returned no matching document for either name. This is a real search of the indexed corpus, stronger than a miss in the local herald-index-full.json, but per CLAUDE.md a miss still proves nothing about a document a search engine has not indexed or an image-only PDF it cannot read - so neither name is closed, only checked and negative on this route.
  Also independently re-verified the 2022 SGA election-night Herald gallery (wkuherald.com/65821), the one clean multi-portrait gallery this project has found in the 2016-2023 gap: all four individually captioned subjects (Cole Bornefeld, Sam Kurtz, Garrison Reed, Holden Schroeder) are already published; none of the current search-list names (Caleb Collins, Barrett Gibbs, Reed Hensley) appear in any of its eight photo captions, only in the running text as election-night senate results, so the gallery has nothing further to give.
